raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On a regex stop, the scheduler records `FINISHED_MATCHED_REGEX(matched=<the pattern source>)` — e.g. `"[0-9]+"` — but the detokenizer trims with a literal `output.find(matched)`. The pattern text almost never occurs in the output, so the find misses and the text is returned **untrimmed**. `no_stop_trim` is unreachable for regex stops (it can neither keep nor remove what was never trimmed), and regex stops behave inconsistently with stop strings, which trim correctly. Fixes #47461.

## Modifications

Two commits, `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`:

- `644881a235` `[Fix] stop_regex: Record the matched span, not the pattern source` — record the matched span instead of the pattern source in `FINISHED_MATCHED_REGEX`.
- `11b64c14d4` `fix: derive the regex span from the emitted prefix` — review follow-up: take the span from `decode(output_ids[:finished_len])` in both branches. The greedy tail match can extend past `finished_len`, and text past it never reaches the detokenizer, so a tail span may not exist in the emitted output.

Net effect: the recorded `matched` string is a span found inside the emitted output, so the detokenizer's literal `output.find(matched)` trims at the first regex match and both `no_stop_trim` branches work. A zero-width span keeps the pattern source — the pre-fix behavior — instead of trimming everything. The detokenizer is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Drove the real `Req.update_finish_state` with a fake tokenizer (pure CPU), same harness as the existing stop-str spec tests:

- With this branch: 20/20 pass — the existing stop-string and stop-regex tests (regression), plus the new non-literal test, which asserts the recorded span is `1` and end-to-end that `trim_matched_stop` trims the emitted `kl1` to `kl`, and a literal-parity guard.
- Against unpatched main with the same test file: the 3 span assertions fail (`matched` is the pattern source there) — the new non-literal test plus the two updated end-anchored assertions. Literal patterns are unaffected on either side (span == pattern text).

Full A/B run on one machine, `pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_stop_str_speculative.py test_trim_matched_stop.py`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference-speed impact: the span derivation runs once per request on the finish path — one `re.search` over the emitted prefix and one decode of it. No hot-path change.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit (ruff format, ruff check --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037, isort, codespell on the changed files).
- [x] Add unit tests (extended `test_stop_str_speculative.py`, including an end-to-end trim assertion; the detokenizer's `trim_matched_stop` needed no change).
- [ ] Documentation (N/A: no user-visible surface changes beyond the trim itself).
- [x] Accuracy results (above); speed N/A.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I think this span can be longer than what actually gets emitted. `group(0)` comes from the whole tail but `finished_len` comes from the shortest prefix that matches, so in your new test `matched` is "123" with `finished_len` 3, and the detokenizer only ever sees "kl1". `"kl1".find("123")` is -1, so the "1" stays in the output, same as on main. Taking the span from `decode(output_ids[:finished_len])` like the end-anchored branch below does would give "1" and trim to "kl".

files.patch:
@@ -2042,8 +2042,23 @@ def _check_str_based_finish(self, new_accepted_len: int = 1):
                     else:
                         finished_len = None
                     if finished_len is not None:
+                        # Record the matched span, not the pattern source:
+                        # the detokenizer trims with a literal find on this
+                        # string, so a non-literal pattern would never be
+                        # found and the output would be returned untrimmed.
+                        # The span must come from the emitted prefix bounded
+                        # by finished_len: the greedy tail match can extend
+                        # past it, and text past it never reaches the
+                        # detokenizer. A zero-width span keeps the pattern
+                        # source (the pre-fix behavior) instead of trimming
+                        # everything.
+                        span = re.search(
+                            stop_regex_str,
+                            self.tokenizer.decode(self.output_ids[:finished_len]),
+                        )
+                        matched_span = span.group(0) if span else None
                         self.finished_reason = FINISHED_MATCHED_REGEX(
-                            matched=stop_regex_str
+                            matched=matched_span or stop_regex_str
                         )
                         self.finished_len = finished_len
                         return True

@@ -7,7 +7,9 @@
 
 import unittest
 from array import array
+from types import SimpleNamespace
 
+from sglang.srt.managers.detokenizer_manager import DetokenizerManager
 from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch import Req
 from sglang.srt.sampling.sampling_params import SamplingParams
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
@@ -28,6 +30,9 @@
     63: ".",
     70: "X",
     71: "Y",
+    80: "1",
+    81: "2",
+    82: "3",
 }
 
 # "STOP" (index 3) sits 6 tokens back: outside the old (stop_str_max_len + 1)
@@ -133,7 +138,7 @@ def test_stop_regex_end_anchored_trims_at_first_match(self):
         req = _make_req([60, 61, 62, 63], stop_regex=[r"\.$"])
         req.update_finish_state(new_accepted_len=4)
         self.assertTrue(req.finished())
-        self.assertEqual(req.finished_reason.matched, r"\.$")
+        self.assertEqual(req.finished_reason.matched, ".")
         self.assertEqual(req.finished_len, 2)
 
     def test_stop_regex_end_anchored_midchunk(self):
@@ -142,9 +147,44 @@ def test_stop_regex_end_anchored_midchunk(self):
         req = _make_req([60, 61, 62], stop_regex=[r"[.!?]\s*$"])
         req.update_finish_state(new_accepted_len=3)
         self.assertTrue(req.finished())
-        self.assertEqual(req.finished_reason.matched, r"[.!?]\s*$")
+        self.assertEqual(req.finished_reason.matched, ".")
         self.assertEqual(req.finished_len, 2)
 
+    # --- the recorded matched string is the span, not the pattern source ---
+    def test_stop_regex_non_literal_records_matched_span(self):
+        # The detokenizer trims with a literal find on `matched`; recording the
+        # pattern source ("[0-9]+") instead of the span left non-literal regex
+        # stops untrimmed and made no_stop_trim unreachable (#47461). The span
+        # must come from the emitted prefix bounded by finished_len: the tail's
+        # greedy match "123" extends past it and is never seen by the
+        # detokenizer, which only gets "kl1".
+        req = _make_req([10, 11, 80, 81, 82, 20], stop_regex=[r"[0-9]+"])
+        req.update_finish_state(new_accepted_len=6)
+        self.assertTrue(req.finished())
+        self.assertEqual(req.finished_reason.to_json()["matched"], "1")
+        self.assertEqual(req.finished_len, 3)
+        # End to end: the detokenizer trims the emitted text at the match.
+        emitted = req.tokenizer.decode(req.output_ids[: req.finished_len])
+        self.assertEqual(emitted, "kl1")
+        stub = SimpleNamespace(
+            is_tool_call_parser_gpt_oss=False, tool_close_token_ids=frozenset()
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            DetokenizerManager.trim_matched_stop(
+                stub, emitted, req.finished_reason.to_json(), False
+            ),
+            "kl",
+        )
+
+    def test_stop_regex_literal_span_equals_pattern(self):
+        # A literal pattern's span is the pattern text itself: identical trim
+        # to the pre-fix behavior.
+        req = _make_req([10, 11, 70, 71, 20], stop_regex=[r"XY"])
+        req.update_finish_state(new_accepted_len=5)
+        self.assertTrue(req.finished())
+        self.assertEqual(req.finished_reason.to_json()["matched"], "XY")
+        self.assertEqual(req.finished_len, 4)
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
